title: Complete local points of algebraic spaces are effective
statement:
Work over a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and a specified morphism $\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Assume that $A\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/\mathfrak m^n$ is an isomorphism of rings. For every algebraic space $B$ over $S$, restriction is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Mor}_S(\operatorname{Spec}A,B)\longrightarrow\varprojlim_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Mor}_S(\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^n),B).$$
The set on the right consists of families $b_n$ with $b_n=b_{n+1}|_{\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^n)}$. Neither separatedness nor a finite-type hypothesis on $B$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0AQH, lemma-map-into-algebraic-space, statement and first displayed equation of its proof.

proof.text: First record the elementary scheme calculation, valid for any complete local ring $(R,\mathfrak n)$ and any scheme $Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring], a compatible family $z_n:\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathfrak n^n)\to Z$ is a common closed-point image $z\in Z$ and compatible local maps $\mathcal O_{Z,z}\to R/\mathfrak n^n$. The inverse-limit isomorphism gives exactly one ring map $\mathcal O_{Z,z}\to R$ with these reductions. It is local: the inverse image of $\mathfrak n$ is the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, as is seen modulo $\mathfrak n$. Applying the same classification gives exactly one morphism $\operatorname{Spec}R\to Z$ with the prescribed restrictions. This also proves injectivity, since reduction modulo $\mathfrak n$ determines $z$ and all reductions determine the stalk map. This calculation is natural in $Z$ and in the local quotient maps, by the explicit stalk-map formula in that classification. For $S$-schemes the result is over $S$: compare the two composites to the scheme $S$ using the injectivity just proved. No Noetherian or separation assumption on $Z$ was used.

source.place: Tag 0AQG (lemma-map-into-scheme), including its omitted injectivity; direct elementary derivation from Schemes Tag 01J6 (lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring).

proof.text: Prove injectivity for the algebraic space $B$, uniformly for every complete Noetherian local $S$-algebra $R$. If $b,c:\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$ have equal reductions, pull back the representable diagonal of [def-trf-algebraic-space] along $(b,c)$ to obtain a scheme $T$ with $T\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ representing their equalizer. By [lem-pc-yoneda], its points over a scheme are exactly maps on which $b$ and $c$ agree. The equal reductions give compatible maps $\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathfrak n^n)\to T$: uniqueness follows because an equalizer is a monomorphism. Step 1 algebraizes them to $t:\operatorname{Spec}R\to T$. Its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ is the identity by the scheme injectivity of step 1. Thus $t$ is a section of the equalizer, so $b=c$. Only representability of the diagonal is needed; no separatedness of $B$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AQH (lemma-map-into-algebraic-space), injectivity paragraph; replace its completed-stalk argument by Tag 0AQG applied to the same scheme equalizer.

proof.text: For surjectivity fix a compatible family $(b_n)$ and put $k=A/\mathfrak m$. Choose a surjective representable etale atlas $U\to B$ with $U$ a scheme, using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $V=U\times_{B,b_1}\operatorname{Spec}k$ is a nonempty scheme etale over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], choose a component $\operatorname{Spec}k'\subset V$, where $k'/k$ is finite separable. Its map to $U$ lifts the restriction of $b_1$ to $k'$.

source.place: Tag 0AQH, surjectivity: choice of U and finite separable k-prime/k (lines 7052–7067); Morphisms Tag 02GL (lemma-etale-over-field).

proof.text: Completeness and [lem-weil-pbc-complete-pair-henselian] make $A$ henselian. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-field-lift] choose a finite etale $A$-algebra $A'$ with $A'/\mathfrak mA'\cong k'$. It is a complete Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m'=\mathfrak mA'$: [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product] writes it as a finite product of complete Noetherian local rings; [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical] puts $\mathfrak mA'$ inside every maximal ideal. Maximal ideals of $A'$ thus correspond to those of the field $A'/\mathfrak mA'$, so there is exactly one and it is $\mathfrak mA'$. There can consequently be only one nonzero local product factor. In particular $\mathfrak m'^n=\mathfrak m^nA'$ for every $n\ge1$.

source.place: Tag 0AQH, finite etale extension R-prime/R; Algebra Tags 04GM, 04GK (lemma-henselian-cat-finite-etale), 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local).

proof.text: Set $A'_n=A'/\mathfrak m^nA'$ and let $b'_n:\operatorname{Spec}A'_n\to B$ be the restriction of $b_n$. Start with the chosen lift $u'_1:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to U$. If $u'_n$ has been constructed over $b'_n$, the closed immersion $\operatorname{Spec}A'_n\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A'_{n+1}$ has square-zero ideal $\mathfrak m^nA'/\mathfrak m^{n+1}A'$, because $2n\ge n+1$. It is a first order thickening of affine $S$-schemes [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. Apply [lem-sfb-etale-space-infinitesimal-lifting] to $U\to B$, $b'_{n+1}$, and $u'_n$ to obtain a unique $u'_{n+1}$ extending $u'_n$ and lying over $b'_{n+1}$. Induction produces a compatible tower $(u'_n)$.

source.place: Tag 0AQH, construction of the compatible u-prime_n (lines 7072–7077); spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tag 0616 (lemma-etale-formally-etale).

proof.text: Apply the scheme calculation of step 1 to $A'$ and $U$ to obtain $u':\operatorname{Spec}A'\to U$ with restrictions $u'_n$. Let $b'$ be its composite to $B$. Thus $b'|_{\operatorname{Spec}A'_n}=b'_n$ for every $n$ by the commuting lifting squares in step 5.

Check descent on $C=A'\otimes_AA'$. It is finite over $A$: products of any two finite module generating sets generate its tensor product. Its spectrum is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, by etale base change and composition [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits, lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-local-product], write $C=\prod_j C_j$ with $C_j$ complete Noetherian local. Each $\mathfrak mC_j$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical], and each local quotient $C_j/\mathfrak mC_j$ is a factor of the finite etale $k$-algebra $C/\mathfrak mC$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product] the latter is a finite product of fields, so each of its nonzero local factors is a field. Consequently $\mathfrak mC_j$ is the maximal ideal of $C_j$. The two pullbacks of $b'$ to $\operatorname{Spec}C_j$ agree modulo $\mathfrak m^nC_j$ for every $n$: both restrictions are the pullback of the original $b_n$, since both $A$-algebra maps $A'\to C_j$ induce the same structural map $A\to C_j$. Apply the injectivity of step 2 to each $C_j$. Hence the two maps on $\operatorname{Spec}C$ agree, using the finite-product spectrum identification [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] and the uniqueness part of the sheaf condition of [def-trf-algebraic-space].

source.place: Tag 0AQH, overlap and injectivity (lines 7080–7090); Algebra Tags 0325 and 00U3. Explicitly identify the maximal ideals on the local factors to justify the use of step 2.

proof.text: Finally $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an fppf covering: it is etale and therefore flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism], and is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat], since $A\to A'$ is flat and local. This meets exactly [def-pc-fppf-site]. The fppf sheaf $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with its points identified with morphisms by [lem-pc-yoneda], therefore descends $b'$ using the equality on the overlap proved in step 7. Obtain $b:\operatorname{Spec}A\to B$. For each $n$, base change of the covering is an fppf covering [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The restriction of $b$ and $b_n$ agree on it, both being $b'_n$; the separatedness part of the sheaf condition makes them equal. This supplies the omitted final compatibility in Tag 0AQH and proves surjectivity. Together with step 2 it proves the stated bijection.

source.place: Tag 0AQH, fppf descent and its omitted final verification (lines 7091–7094); Topologies Tag 021L (definition-fppf-covering); Sites Tag 00VM (definition-sheaf).

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q40-db64346a4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Stacks formal-spaces.tex Tags 0AQH and 0AQG in full. The item statement is unchanged from live (unsplit) and matches 0AQH. There is no repair note and no parallel split. All 8 steps are correct and each cited statement says what the step takes from it. Step 1: scheme case from morphism-from-spec-local-ring plus completeness; locality via φ_1; the over-S property by injectivity at Z=S; elementary. Step 2: injectivity via the representable-diagonal equalizer scheme T (a monomorphism by Yoneda); step 1 gives a section t with p∘t=id, so b=c without the source's lft/completed-stalk argument. Step 3: the atlas fibre over b_1 is etale and surjective over k, and one point Spec k' is taken from it. Step 4: A' is henselian-lifted with A'/mA'≅k' as κ-algebras; local-radical forces a unique maximal ideal mA', so there is one complete factor. Step 5: m^{2n}⊂m^{n+1} gives first-order thickenings; the lifting is applied to the atlas with the base case explicit. Step 6: algebraize u'. Step 7: C=A'⊗A' is finite and etale over A, so a product of complete local C_j; mC_j is maximal because C/mC is a product of fields; both pullbacks reduce to b_n∘(A→C_j), so step 2 applies per factor, then the coproduct spectrum and sheaf uniqueness finish. Step 8: the fppf covering is etale and surjective by flat-local; descent, then the source-omitted compatibility b|_{A_n}=b_n via the base-changed covering. Edge cases checked: m=0, nilpotent m, nontrivial k'/k, several C_j, non-separated B, empty B. Duplicate search on 0AQH/0AQG found only the parent node; no SGA cited. Tool_uses: trf fibre products is off-route and accepted as generic; the pbc entries are on-route via sk-thm-p1.
